name: dialogue30
closers: Write the team a detailed note of about 1500 words on what we decided so far in this conversation and why. Answer here, do not write a file.
Write the team a note of about 600 words on this last topic only, with what to do next. Answer here, do not write a file.

says: We are adding a queue for invoice events. Invent a name for it, two lowercase words joined by a hyphen, nothing we have used in this conversation. Put it on a line of its own as QUEUE=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Pick how many hours the dead-letter queue keeps a message, any whole number between 30 and 300 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as RETENTION=<hours>, then your reason.
Every message id needs a prefix of four uppercase letters. Choose one. Put it on a line of its own as PREFIX=<letters>.
Different topic. Draft a 120 word message to the team saying stand-up moves half an hour later from next week.
List five questions you would ask a candidate for a platform engineering role, one line each.
Explain the difference between a mutex and a semaphore in one paragraph, for a junior engineer.

chains.lead: Back to the first things we decided in this conversation, about the invoice events queue.

questions.ask: What name did you give the queue?
How many hours does the dead-letter queue keep a message?
Which prefix did you choose for message ids?

says: We launch the new checkout next month and need a codename for it. Invent one, two lowercase words joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as CODENAME=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
What share of traffic should the canary take? Any whole number of percent between 11 and 89 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as CANARY=<percent>, then your reason.
Name the feature flag that gates it: three lowercase words joined by underscores. Put it on a line of its own as FLAG=<name>.
Different topic. Write a short agenda for a one hour retrospective, with a time box per item.
Suggest three ways to make code review faster without lowering the bar, one line each.
Explain what an idempotency key is and when an API needs one, in one paragraph.

chains.lead: Back to the checkout launch we planned first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What codename did you invent for the launch?
What share of traffic did you give the canary, in percent?
What is the name of the feature flag that gates it?

says: We are adding a read replica for reporting. Give it a name: a mineral followed by two digits, lowercase, joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as REPLICA=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Pick the connection pool size for it, any whole number between 37 and 213 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as POOL=<size>, then your reason.
Choose the start of the nightly backup window, any minute of the day in UTC as HH:MM. Put it on a line of its own as WINDOW=<HH:MM>.
Different topic. Draft a 100 word welcome note for a new engineer joining on Monday.
Give me four signs a service is ready to be split in two, one line each.
Explain eventual consistency to a product manager in one paragraph, with an everyday example.

chains.lead: Back to the reporting read replica we set up first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What name did you give the read replica?
What connection pool size did you pick?
At what time UTC does the backup window start?

says: We are starting a pager rotation for the payments team. Invent a name for the rotation, two lowercase words joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as ROTATION=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Pick the timeout for the payment provider client in milliseconds, any whole number between 1200 and 9800 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as TIMEOUT=<ms>, then your reason.
Give the runbook an id: RB- followed by three digits of your choice. Put it on a line of its own as RUNBOOK=<id>.
Different topic. Write a 120 word note asking the team to fill in the quarterly survey.
List four things a good pull request description says, one line each.
Explain backpressure in a streaming system in one paragraph, for a junior engineer.

chains.lead: Back to the payments pager rotation we set up first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What name did you give the rotation?
What timeout did you pick for the provider client, in milliseconds?
What id did you give the runbook?

says: We are adding a plan between free and pro. Invent its name, one capitalised word that is not a common English word. Put it on a line of its own as PLAN=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Set its monthly price in cents, any whole number between 1000 and 9999 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as PRICE=<cents>, then your reason.
Make a launch coupon code of eight characters, uppercase letters and digits. Put it on a line of its own as COUPON=<code>.
Different topic. Draft a 100 word reply to a customer who asks why an export took an hour.
List five metrics you would put on a dashboard for a public API, one line each.
Explain the difference between a feature flag and a configuration setting in one paragraph.

chains.lead: Back to the new plan we priced first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What did you name the plan?
What monthly price did you set, in cents?
What is the launch coupon code?

says: Our test suite is too slow and we will shard it. Pick a fixed random seed for the shard assignment, any whole number between 10000 and 99999. Put it on a line of its own as SEED=<number>, then one sentence on why fixing it matters. Do not change any file.
How many shards should we start with? Any whole number between 5 and 61 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as SHARDS=<count>, then your reason.
Invent the CI label that triggers the sharded run, two lowercase words joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as LABEL=<label>.
Different topic. Write a short checklist for handing over on-call at the end of a week.
Suggest three names for an internal newsletter, one line each, and pick your favourite.
Explain what a flaky test costs a team, in one paragraph, without numbers.

chains.lead: Back to the test sharding we planned first in this conversation.

questions.ask: Which seed did you pick for the shard assignment?
How many shards did we start with?
What CI label triggers the sharded run?

says: We are adding an endpoint for bulk refunds. Invent the path segment for it, one lowercase word that is not refund, refunds or bulk. Put it on a line of its own as SEGMENT=<word>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Set its rate limit in requests per minute, any whole number between 140 and 990 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as LIMIT=<number>, then your reason.
Name the request header that carries the batch id: X- followed by two capitalised words joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as HEADER=<name>.
Different topic. Draft a 120 word note announcing a no-meeting Wednesday.
List four questions to ask before adding a new dependency, one line each.
Explain optimistic locking in one paragraph, with an example from a shop.

chains.lead: Back to the bulk refund endpoint we designed first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What path segment did you invent for the endpoint?
What rate limit did you set, in requests per minute?
What is the name of the header that carries the batch id?

says: We need a storage bucket for exported reports. Invent its name, three lowercase words joined by hyphens. Put it on a line of its own as BUCKET=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
After how many days should an export be deleted? Any whole number between 45 and 400 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as DAYS=<number>, then your reason.
Name the encryption key alias: alias/ followed by one lowercase word, a hyphen and two digits. Put it on a line of its own as ALIAS=<alias>.
Different topic. Write a 100 word note thanking the support team for a busy month.
Suggest four ways to cut the time a new engineer takes to ship a first change, one line each.
Explain what a write-ahead log is for, in one paragraph.

chains.lead: Back to the bucket for exported reports we set up first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What name did you give the bucket?
After how many days is an export deleted?
What is the encryption key alias?

says: We are moving to release trains. Invent a name for the first train, one capitalised made-up word. Put it on a line of its own as TRAIN=<name>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
How long should the code freeze before each train last, in hours? Any whole number between 19 and 71 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as FREEZE=<hours>, then your reason.
Give the first train's build tag as v<major>.<minor>.<patch>, each number between 2 and 19, your choice. Put it on a line of its own as TAG=<tag>.
Different topic. Draft a 120 word note inviting the team to a lunch and learn on observability.
List five things to check before deleting an old database table, one line each.
Explain the difference between latency and throughput in one paragraph, with a road analogy.

chains.lead: Back to the release trains we planned first in this conversation.

questions.ask: What name did you invent for the first train?
How long is the code freeze, in hours?
What build tag did you give the first train?

says: We are redesigning the docs site. Pick its accent colour as a six digit hex code with a leading hash. Put it on a line of its own as COLOR=<hex>, then one sentence on why. Do not change any file.
Invent the name of the new sidebar section for migration guides, two lowercase words joined by a hyphen. Put it on a line of its own as SECTION=<name>, then your reason.
How many shards should the docs search index have? Any whole number between 3 and 29 that you can defend. Put it on a line of its own as INDEXSHARDS=<count>.
Different topic. Write a 100 word note asking for volunteers to mentor interns.
List four habits that keep a changelog useful, one line each.
Explain what a content delivery network does in one paragraph, for a designer.

chains.lead: Back to the docs site redesign we planned first in this conversation.

questions.ask: Which accent colour did you pick, as a hex code?
What did you name the new sidebar section?
How many shards did you give the search index?
